Boundary Police District Assistant Commander (Operations and Crime) Superintendent Chan Kai-chak said that at 4:12pm today, police received a report that a local woman was found lying unconscious on the grass outside House 111, Ping Yeung Village. Police and paramedics arrived at the scene and found the woman, with a stray mongrel wandering nearby. Paramedics examined her and confirmed her death.

Chan Kai-chak said the Boundary Police District Crime Unit has taken over the investigation. The scene is a licensed pet hotel and dog training centre that began operating in January this year, with no signs of robbery. After reviewing CCTV footage, police found that at around 2pm, the woman was feeding the mongrel on the outdoor grass and attempted to put the dog back in its cage shortly after. The dog refused to enter and attacked the woman.

Police said the final CCTV footage showed the woman and the mongrel leaving the kennel and walking toward the grass area. Police said the deceased was a 33-year-old woman and the licensee of the pet hotel, and she was the only person working at the hotel at the time of the incident. The deceased sustained varying degrees of lacerations and animal bite wounds to her head, jaw, neck, and both arms. The mongrel involved is a one-year-old male, brought in for boarding by a dog volunteer on August 11 this year, hoping it would be adopted. Personnel from the forensic pathologist, the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA), the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD), and the Labour Department assisted at the scene. The mongrel will be taken away by the AFCD.

Police said they will investigate whether there were any violations or negligence in the incident. Police said the dog attacked the woman while she was still alive, and both the woman and the dog subsequently left the kennel and went to the grass area outside. The cause of death is pending confirmation by autopsy. The deceased was conscious when attacked, and the mongrel's attack lasted approximately one minute. The dog is about one metre in length. There were six other dogs at the scene, all of which were inside cages at the time.
